title: Why Is a Day on Venus LONGER Than Its Year? 🎂
description:
On Venus, one day lasts longer than a whole year. Venus is the slowest-spinning planet of all: it goes once round the Sun in about 225 Earth days, but it takes 243 Earth days to turn around once on its own axis. So you'd have a birthday before Venus had turned around even once. And it spins backwards (the opposite way to Earth), so the Sun comes up in the west. Bonus: because of that backwards spin, sunrise to sunrise is "only" about 117 Earth days. Would you want a 243-day Monday? Yes or no?
